info.name: Vinay Bank API
info.description:
Ready-to-run requests for the Vinay Bank REST API.

**How to use**
1. Start the project: `npm run dev` (API on http://localhost:4000).
2. Run the folders from top to bottom. "1. Sign in" saves the access token; later requests reuse it automatically.
3. Every request has a description and a few automatic checks (the **Test Results** tab).

For the Docker version (`docker compose up -d`), select the **Vinay Bank (Docker)** environment: it points `baseUrl` at http://localhost:8080/api/v1.

The sign-in values are the demo accounts from the README; they only exist in your local demo database.

item.name: 0. Start here
item.description: Is the API awake? These two requests need no sign-in.

request.description: The simplest possible request. If this works, the API is running and Postman can reach it.

exec: pm.test('The API says it is ok', () => pm.expect(body.data.status).to.equal('ok'));
pm.test('It is the Vinay Bank API', () => pm.expect(body.data.service).to.equal('Vinay Bank API'));

request.description: Like the health check, but the API also pings MongoDB before answering.

item.name: 1. Sign in
item.description: Get an access token. The script in "Login as customer" stores it, so every later request is signed in.

request.description:
Sends the email and password. The answer contains a short-lived **access token** (15 minutes) and sets an httpOnly **refresh cookie** (see the Cookies tab).

The Scripts tab saves the token into the `accessToken` variable.

exec: pm.test('We are signed in as a customer', () => pm.expect(body.data.user.role).to.equal('CUSTOMER'));

request.description: Uses the saved token (Authorization: Bearer ...). The API reads who you are from the token.
Every sign-in creates a session. This lists them (the app shows this under Profile and security).

header.description: Proves the call comes from our own page (CSRF defence for cookie endpoints)

request.description: No token in this request: the **cookie** proves who you are. The API swaps the old refresh cookie for a new one (rotation) and returns a fresh access token.

exec: pm.test('A new access token came back', () => pm.expect(body.data.accessToken).to.be.a('string'));

item.name: 2. Accounts
item.description: Read-only requests about the customer's accounts.

request.description: Lists the accounts with balances **in paise** (24503000 means Rs 2,45,030.00). The script remembers the first two account ids.

exec: pm.test('Balances are whole numbers of paise', () => pm.expect(Number.isInteger(accounts[0].ledgerBalance)).to.equal(true));

request.description: Everything the dashboard shows in one call: totals, this month, cash flow and spending by category.
Details of the first account. Try another customer's account id: the API answers 404, because it checks ownership.
A paginated list. Look at `meta` in the answer: page, limit, total, totalPages.

exec: pm.test('Five rows on this page', () => pm.expect(body.data.length).to.equal(5));

request.description: The same data as a spreadsheet file. Not JSON: look at the Content-Type header.
The same data as XML (accounting software likes XML).
The API calls a public service (European Central Bank rates) and caches the answer.

item.name: 3. Send money
item.description: A complete transfer in the same two steps the web app uses: quote, then execute with the OTP.

request.description: Saved payees. The script picks Rahul (a Vinay Bank customer, so the transfer is instant and free).

exec: pm.test('Found a payee to pay', () => pm.expect(rahul).to.be.an('object'));

request.description: Every Indian bank branch has an IFSC code. The API asks a public directory and remembers the answer.

Asks: "what would it cost to send Rs 250 to Rahul?" Nothing moves yet. The API checks the balance and limits, scores the fraud risk, sends an OTP and returns a signed **quote token**.

Amounts are in paise: 25000 = Rs 250.00.

exec: pm.test('Vinay Bank to Vinay Bank is free', () => pm.expect(quote.fee).to.equal(0));
// One key per transfer attempt: sending it twice must never pay twice.

request.description: A real bank sends the OTP by SMS. In demo mode it arrives as an in-app notification, so we can read it here. The script copies the 6 digits into the `otp` variable.

header.description: Unique per transfer attempt; makes retries safe

request.description: Confirms the quote with the OTP. The debit, the credit, both statement lines and the transaction record are written in **one database transaction**: all of it happens or none of it.

item.name: Step 2 again (same key: no second payment)

header.description: The same key as the previous request

request.description: Imagine the network dropped and the app retried. Because the **Idempotency-Key** is the same, the API returns the original result instead of paying twice. Look for the `Idempotent-Replayed: true` header.

exec: pm.test('The API says this is a replay', () => pm.expect(pm.response.headers.get('Idempotent-Replayed')).to.equal('true'));

request.description: The transfer you just made is at the top.
Full details, including the fraud risk score the engine gave it.

item.name: 4. Cards and the ATM network
item.description: Debit cards, and a real ISO 8583 message sent through the card switch.

request.description: The card number is masked. The full number needs an OTP (try the web app).
Only available in demo mode: the card number and expiry an ATM would read from the chip.

item.name: ATM balance inquiry (ISO 8583 through the switch)

request.description: The API acts as an ATM: it builds an ISO 8583 message (type 0200), encrypts the PIN into a PIN block, adds a MAC and sends it over mutual TLS to the card switch, which asks the issuer. The answer shows both messages field by field.

exec: pm.test('The link used TLS 1.2 or newer', () => pm.expect(result.exchange.tls.protocol).to.match(/^TLSv1\.[23]$/));

item.name: 5. Staff (manager)
item.description: Signs in as the branch manager. This folder uses its own token (`staffToken`), so the customer stays signed in too.

request.description: Same endpoint, different person. The role in the answer is MANAGER.
Numbers for the staff dashboard, calculated inside MongoDB with aggregation pipelines. Also reports whether the Java risk engine is up.
Maker-checker: requests waiting for a second person.
Finds customers whose name starts with "pri".
Staff see every customer's transactions; a customer sees only their own. Same URL, different answer, because of the role in the token.
Recomputes the SHA-256 hash chain over every audit record. `valid: true` means nobody edited history.
From the SQL ledger: total debits must equal total credits.
Compares every account balance in MongoDB with the SQL ledger.
Health of the Spring Boot service and the state of the circuit breaker (CLOSED means healthy).

item.name: 6. Errors on purpose
item.description: Things that should fail. Each test checks that the API refuses politely, with a clear error code.

request.description: No Authorization header. 401 means "I do not know who you are".

exec: pm.test('Every error carries a request id for the logs', () => pm.expect(body.requestId).to.be.a('string'));

request.description: The message is the same whether the email exists or not, so nobody can discover which emails are registered.

exec: pm.test('Every error carries a request id for the logs', () => pm.expect(body.requestId).to.be.a('string'));

request.description: A negative amount and an id that is not an id. Look at `error.details`: one entry per wrong field.

exec: pm.test('Every error carries a request id for the logs', () => pm.expect(body.requestId).to.be.a('string'));
pm.test('The answer lists the wrong fields', () => pm.expect(body.error.details.map((d) => d.field)).to.include('amount'));

request.description: Signed in, but as a customer. 403 means "I know who you are, and you may not do this".

exec: pm.test('Every error carries a request id for the logs', () => pm.expect(body.requestId).to.be.a('string'));

request.description: Nothing lives at this address.

exec: pm.test('Every error carries a request id for the logs', () => pm.expect(body.requestId).to.be.a('string'));

request.description: The body stops in the middle. The API still answers with the same tidy error shape.

exec: pm.test('Every error carries a request id for the logs', () => pm.expect(body.requestId).to.be.a('string'));

request.description: Money-moving requests must carry an Idempotency-Key header.

exec: pm.test('Every error carries a request id for the logs', () => pm.expect(body.requestId).to.be.a('string'));

request.description: Cookie endpoints demand the X-Requested-With header, which a form on another website cannot send (CSRF defence).

exec: pm.test('Every error carries a request id for the logs', () => pm.expect(body.requestId).to.be.a('string'));

item.name: 7. Sign out
item.description: Signs in once more, signs out, and proves the old token no longer works.

request.description: Folder 5 signed in as the manager, which replaced the cookie (one cookie jar, one cookie name). Signing in again makes the cookie and the token belong to the same customer session, exactly as in a browser.

header.description: Proves the call comes from our own page (CSRF defence for cookie endpoints)

request.description: Revokes the session and clears the refresh cookie. 204 means "done, nothing to say".
The access token has not expired yet, but its **session was revoked**, so the API refuses it immediately. This is why the guard checks the session on every request.

exec: pm.test('Every error carries a request id for the logs', () => pm.expect(body.requestId).to.be.a('string'));
